cells.tense: You are carrying what you chose when it was new, and the carry is steady now.
cells.ask: Tell one person one reason you keep going, and don't promise it'll work. Notice a reason was ready.
cells.core:
You picked this up a long time ago and you're still holding it. Not gripping it — holding it. The difference shows in how you rest. You can set it down at night and pick it back up and it doesn't fall apart in between.

This is the weathered kind of strength. Not the loud kind that gets you through one bad week — the quiet kind that survives a decade. From where you're looking you can see the whole shape of it: what it cost, what it made, what's left. None of it was easy and you're not pretending it was. Persistence here doesn't mean forcing. It means holding without squeezing.
cells.sheetLine: You've carried this a long time and it hasn't worn you down.
cells.verb: keeping on with what you hoped for long after the hoping got quiet
cells.place: standing back far enough to see the whole of it at once

cells.tense: You are already bracing for the day this gives out, and you are carrying that day around now.
cells.ask: Write down the outcome you're bracing for, with a date. Then stop planning for that date for one week.
cells.core:
Somewhere ahead you see the whole thing collapsing, and you're getting ready for it now. Talks turn into fortification. A quiet moment becomes a scan for what's about to give. The bracing feels like care. It looks like foresight. And it costs you the thing it's protecting.

Done well, this strength just carries what's here: you hold through a hard week because you've held before, and the sight of the whole pattern tells you what's still turning. The excess turns the pattern into a forecast and the forecast into armor. Persistence can't run that far ahead of the thing it's for. The part that rests easy, that lets a perception land without an answer already wrapped around it — that's what to lean back toward.
cells.sheetLine: You're spending today's strength on a day that hasn't shown up.

cells.tense: You stopped carrying what you hoped for a while back, and you have not picked it up.
cells.ask: Pick one small piece of that old thing and do fifteen minutes of it today. Not to decide anything — just to see your hands on it.
cells.core:
You set it down back there somewhere and you haven't gone back for it. That's not laziness. Going back means touching the whole thing, and the whole thing is a lot. Easier not to look. Easier to stay where no looking is needed.

The persistence you're known for runs quieter now. It's still in you — you can feel it in other parts of your life, tending what needs tending. It just isn't pointed at the thing you hoped for. That gap isn't a verdict on you. It's a door, and you don't have to walk through it today. Looking is allowed.

cells.tense: You are already holding the whole pattern together right now, and you call it keeping things running.
cells.ask: Name one thing you do to keep this going and claim it quietly, once, as your own.
cells.core:
You already see the whole shape of it — what holds, what's cracking, what will need tending in three weeks. You adjust without deciding to. You take the shock before anyone else feels it. From the outside it looks like things just work.

But you don't count that as yours. You call it logistics. You call it keeping up. The person doing the work is the person not getting credit for it — and what's underway is patient strength under pressure, practiced so long it runs without a sound. That kind of strength is steady. You're allowed to notice you're the one providing it.
cells.sheetLine: You're the one holding it together and you call it nothing.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that this persistence has been consciously chosen and faith-held by the person. A reader could reasonably say: it has been endurance under pressure, not aspiration, and I don't experience hope in it. The ask (tell someone why you keep going, without promising anything) is still useful if the read is wrong about why they persist, because it teaches what language could carry. The sentence that serves the writer more than them is any claim that the person 'kept the faith' — it flatters the brand of the card and is not in the print.
